summary: DSE/Fiji R27 replaces the former single main 24 V enclosure with a battery-adjacent cutoff box, an external guarded main-distribution cluster and a secondary-services box. The cutoff box contains only the purchased string A, string B and SmartSolar 120 A disconnects in the verified-fit HT-8. The purchased Joinfworld 250 A four-stud positive/negative buses remain outside with their supplied covers installed; main-positive lug stacking is accepted. The adjacent IP65 SmartShunt remains uncovered and all battery-negative current passes through it. The verified-fit 302 × 302 × 178 mm secondary box contains the generic 10 A shared-services branch position, purchased 32 A Orion and ChargeIT breakers, allocated Blue Sea 2314 positive/negative buses, six-gang switch panel, USB-C converter and Starlink power routing. Supplemental correctly terminated 1/0 AWG cable will be purchased onsite. Source-side protection, feeder ampacity and the 100 A secondary buses must still be coordinated before energizing.

powerModel.assumptions: 4.2 peak-sun-hours, 75% solar derate, 50% GEL depth of discharge, one power tool at a time, about 0.10 kWh/day for the always-on Ekrano GX with its display normally asleep, and 15 m one-way copper PV runs. PV cable loss uses 0.01724 Ω·mm²/m copper resistivity at 20°C; field temperature raises resistance, so confirm the actual route and cable before purchase. The 590 W USB figure is simultaneous output capacity, not an added daily-energy assumption. With ORION REMOTE H enabled but no devices connected, the Orion data-sheet maximum no-load draw plus four ChargeIT idle loads is below about 2.64 W / 0.064 kWh per day; remote-off draw is below about 0.0006 kWh per day, excluding the small rocker LED. Coolgear does not publish the 145 W charger's idle draw, so measure each received unit. R27 retains the purchased dedicated 32 A positive-branch breakers for the Orion input and four-module ChargeIT chain plus the selected-to-buy generic 10 A shared-services branch. Coordinate the source-side protection, secondary feeder ampacity and both 100 A secondary buses before energizing. Use ORION REMOTE H to shut down the 145 W socket branch and verify the downstream 12 V harness protection separately.

batteryCablePlan.planningRule: Each planning length adds at least 10% to the final R27 routed centerline and then rounds upward to the next 0.05 m. It is a minimum procurement/mock-up allowance, not a cut instruction; increase it wherever the received terminal body, bend radius, support spacing or service loop requires more.

sourceLeadComparison.definition: Four battery-post source leads only: string A/B positive to the cutoff inputs plus string A/B negative to SmartShunt BATTERY MINUS; series links and protected downstream conductors are excluded.

batteryCablePlan.inventoryAllocationStatus: Accepted procurement plan: allocate the fixed purchased assemblies only where their received length, lug geometry and conductor markings match the final supported route, then purchase the remaining correctly terminated red and black 1/0 AWG cable onsite in Fiji. A 2 ft / 0.61 m nominal piece is not automatically assigned to the 0.62 m source lead or any 0.58 m routed path because termination take-up, bends and service slack can make it too short. Both 1.64 m / 1.46 m MultiPlus feeds and the 1.64 m secondary return require onsite cable; source/protection and #10-32 transition coordination remains on hold for the secondary feeder pair. The equal red/black purchased-pair inventory does not match the routed demand by polarity, so the final onsite quantity follows received-part allocation rather than a gross-length subtraction.
batteryCablePlan.measurementRule: Use the routed centerlines only as geometry evidence. Mock up the received batteries, DIHOOL cutoff devices, external SmartShunt, Joinfworld buses and MultiPlus at full size; measure along the supported conductor path and verify terminal take-up, service slack, bend radius, lug orientation and paired-path requirements before selecting or ordering an assembly. Battery and MultiPlus posts require M8 while the purchased assemblies have 3/8 in / M10 rings, and the DIHOOL/SmartSolar devices use clamp terminals; use only approved terminations or transitions. Never trim strands, drill lugs or claim UL 1426/tinned-marine construction without received markings.

operatingRules: Keep both PV strings on their separate 4 mm² positive/negative home runs all the way to the indoor entry enclosure. Do not combine at the array or substitute MC4 branch leads; this revision deliberately removes the one-run fallback and the outdoor combiner.

Use one corded power tool at a time from the dedicated trailing socket and keep the tool nameplate at or below about 1,800 W. Fully uncoil and inspect the lead before use; do not add a power board, daisy-chain another extension, or combine the saw with the planer, jigsaw, drill, kettle or another large AC load. Hang the lead dry beside the equipment after use.
Run tool work mainly in sunny hours. Stop tool loads around 50% state of charge; reserve the lower half of the GEL bank for longevity and essentials.

Keep the AC inverter off when no AC loads are required. Use STARLINK + UNIFI to shut down Starlink and UniFi overnight, and use ORION REMOTE H to put the Orion below 1 mA remote-off standby. The four breaker-protected ChargeIT Minis have no remote shutoff; measure their combined idle draw and open their 32 A branch breaker when long-term shutdown is needed.
Leave the Ekrano GX powered so it can retain battery history and report alarms. Let its display time out when not in use; investigate alarms locally before resetting them.

Keep both internal 120 A battery-string breakers ON in normal service only after the received DIHOOL devices pass documented DC-rating, interrupt-capacity, terminal and acceptance checks. Switch both OFF after AC loads, MultiPlus, PV and generator charging are shut down. Battery fault energy remains substantial.

If a battery or balancer alarm suggests a bad string: shut down every load and charge source, switch both string breakers OFF, verify individual battery and string voltages with a multimeter, and disconnect and insulate both leads of the diagnosed bad string. Only then may the healthy string's breaker be returned ON. Reduce the Ekrano DVCC charge-current limit from 100 A to 50 A. A single healthy 200 Ah string can still operate one ordinary power tool, but runtime and surge headroom are roughly halved: work in sun, monitor voltage and temperature, and stop immediately on excessive sag, alarm or breaker trip.
Never equalize GEL batteries. Inspect individual battery voltage, temperature, swelling, torque and corrosion monthly.

Keep all power electronics dry and away from direct salt air. Every three months, isolate the system, inspect for salt deposits or corrosion, clean/replace the alcove filter and correct any moisture source.

Treat the generator as tested backup only. Have the qualified installer verify the accepted AC-input assembly, generator neutral-earth arrangement and coordination between the input and output 30 mA devices. Keep AC-in N and AC-out N isolated; only protective earth is common, through the continuous unswitched PE chain. Do not add a permanent N–PE link in the AC box.

AC neutral and PE are not interchangeable. Neutral carries normal load return current; PE normally carries no current and remains continuously bonded for fault protection. Never switch PE, never use PE as a neutral, and never add a permanent N–PE link in the AC box—the MultiPlus ground relay manages the output bond.
commissioning: Confirm all four panel and battery nameplates before terminating anything.

Allocate the nine purchased fixed-length 1/0 AWG red/black pairs (18 individual cables, 27 conductor-feet) only where received length, conductor markings and lug geometry match the verified route. Purchase the remaining correctly terminated red and black 1/0 AWG cable onsite in Fiji, including both MultiPlus feeds. Bench-check the DIHOOL clamps, battery M8 posts, SmartShunt M10 studs, Joinfworld studs and MultiPlus M8 posts; reject any forced bend or incompatible lug.
Separately fully charge and voltage-match the four batteries. Build two matched 24 V strings, install one balancer per string, and land each balancer alarm relay on its own Ekrano digital input.

Fit exactly the two selected non-polarized DIHOOL 120 A battery-string breakers plus the SmartSolar 120 A cutoff in the verified HT-8 battery-adjacent enclosure. Confirm received DC markings, interrupt rating, terminal capacity and torque. Wall-mount the four-stud main buses outside all enclosures with their supplied covers installed; leave the adjacent IP65 SmartShunt uncovered. Route both battery negatives only to SmartShunt BATTERY MINUS and SmartShunt SYSTEM MINUS to the main negative bus. Build the approved main-positive lug stacks with specified torque and adequate thread engagement, and document the installed conductor order.

With modules covered, build two independent two-panel series strings. Uncover and measure about 100.8 V Voc at 25°C on each string separately; confirm close agreement, polarity, labels and isolation before landing all four 4 mm² home-run conductors. Parallel them only at the protected indoor building-entry terminals, then confirm the SmartSolar's 100 A protected battery branch before closing the 40 A PV disconnect.

Use the two purchased 20 A common-trip two-pole CHTAIXI devices as the planned PV string breakers only after received-marking, polarity, cold-Voc, interrupt-rating and local-acceptance checks. Keep the older 32 A pair out of the design and return it.

Program MultiPlus and SmartSolar for the exact GEL label; planning values are 28.2 V absorption, 27.2 V float and equalization disabled. Install the temperature sensor supplied with the 24 V MultiPlus on Battery 1's negative terminal. In Ekrano DVCC, select the SmartShunt for Shared Voltage Sense and Shared Current Sense, select the MultiPlus sensor for Shared Temperature Sense, and set the system-wide charge-current limit to 100 A with both strings healthy. Do not add a Smart Battery Sense unless this wired sensing path is later removed or proves unusable.

Return or exchange the incompatible SCC950400300 / MC4 WireBox unopened. Obtain SCC950400210 WireBox-XL Tr for the purchased SmartSolar 150/85-Tr VE.Can, verify both part-number labels and install per Victron's quick guide.
Set the MultiPlus to 230 V / 50 Hz with a 10 A AC input-current limit for the G3200P; verify generator acceptance before enabling unattended charging.

With the 24 V bank isolated, install the accepted verified-fit HT-8 battery/MPPT cutoff enclosure and nominal 302 × 302 × 178 mm ABS secondary-services enclosure in their R27 wall positions. Preserve the verified breaker access, bends, guarded terminals, vent sealing, cable entries and shortest-practical 1/0 AWG battery leads.

Power the Ekrano directly from the protected 24 V bus with its supplied 3.15 A slow-blow fused lead, with negative on the system side of the SmartShunt. Never power it from MultiPlus AC-out or from the voltage-controlled DC-load branch.

Connect the MultiPlus by Victron RJ45 UTP/VE.Bus, SmartSolar and SmartShunt by separate VE.Direct cables, both balancer alarm relays to separate Ekrano digital inputs, and Ekrano Ethernet to the UniFi Express LAN port. Confirm all three Victron devices, SmartShunt battery state, battery temperature, SVS/SCS/STS sources and both balancer alarms appear locally.

Register the Ekrano in VRM over UniFi/Starlink, enable HTTPS and two-factor authentication on administrator accounts, configure useful battery/temperature/offline alarms, set a connection-appropriate log interval, and test both local operation without internet and remote recovery after reconnect.
Set the Ekrano display auto-off timer and adaptive brightness, record the VRM Portal ID and access recovery details off-site, and export configuration backups before departure.
Torque to each manufacturer specification; re-torque after the first week and mark fasteners with witness paint.

Keep both purchased Mollom HT-8 units out of the installed AC assembly. Install the separately tracked second HT-8 as the verified-fit R27 three-device battery/MPPT cutoff enclosure; retain the first as an owned spare. The two purchased DIHOOL 10 A ground-fault/surge units are AC-in and AC-out candidates only after exact 10 A, 30 mA Type A, SPD classification, L/N/PE arrangement, interrupt rating, 230 V / 50 Hz suitability and qualified-installer acceptance are confirmed. No unselected replacement AC-enclosure allowance remains in the BOM; add only the actual AC enclosure after its separate fit check.

Route four separate three-core cables through the AC enclosure: generator → input LINE, input LOAD → MultiPlus AC-in, MultiPlus AC-out-1 → output LINE, and output LOAD → Type I trailing socket. Keep the two neutrals segregated. Daisy-chain PE only through dedicated unswitched PE pass-through terminals rated for the exact conductor count: generator → input protector → MultiPlus chassis/PE → output protector → socket, with the main PE bond joined at the input PE node. If any received terminal cannot do this, use a larger enclosure and approved PE terminal block.

Cut the purchased six-gang panel opening at the accepted secondary-services enclosure face/cover location from the verified layout. Label the vertical rockers, top to bottom: STARLINK + UNIFI; OUTDOOR LIGHT; ORION REMOTE H; SPARE; SPARE; SPARE. Gasket the perimeter, insulate every rear terminal and verify the protected daisy-chain conductors. Switch 3 carries only the Orion H-pin control signal; L is unused and USB charging current bypasses the switch panel.

Secure two genuine WAGO 221-413 connectors in proper carriers inside the secondary-services enclosure. The first splits the selected generic 10 A shared-services branch between the six-gang common feed and remote room-switch run. The second splits the STARLINK + UNIFI switch output between the Starlink bulkhead jack and dedicated UniFi converter. Connect Starlink Ethernet directly to the UniFi Express WAN port and bench-test at least ten simultaneous Starlink/UniFi power cycles.

Use QHLightlux B0F1V59NXC 3000 K fixtures for both locations. Suspend the indoor unit from a short dry bracket with its lens down; mount the outdoor unit under an eave with 316 stainless fasteners and sealed bedding. Put two 3 A silicon rectifier diodes in series with each switched positive branch. Route one protected positive from the secondary-services enclosure to one pole of the IP66 DPST switch beside the opposite doorway, one switched positive onward to the indoor fixture, and one direct unswitched negative from the secondary negative bus to the fixture. Dress all three long conductors along the ceiling, cap the unused pole and verify the received contact diagram before energizing.

Bench-test the Starlink Mini from the 24 V branch through its complete OEM 15 m cable: verify center-positive polarity at the bulkhead jack, cold-start it at low battery voltage, and confirm STARLINK + UNIFI simultaneously removes Starlink and UniFi without interrupting the independently switched USB or lights.

Run the 1,800 W saw alone for 30 minutes in warm conditions with the 5 m lead fully uncoiled while monitoring inverter, lead, plug/socket, cable and terminal temperature; post the one-page operating rules and breaker map beside the equipment.

Continuity-test the complete AC PE chain with each protection device ON and OFF. Prove low-resistance continuity from generator earth and the main PE bond to MultiPlus chassis and the Type I socket, prove no input-neutral/output-neutral cross-connection, and test the MultiPlus ground-relay behavior in inverter and generator/bypass modes before energizing the socket.

Build the R27 secondary-services rail with exactly three branch positions: the to-be-selected generic 10 A shared-services breaker, purchased 32 A Orion input breaker and purchased 32 A ChargeIT breaker. No make or part number is yet approved for the 10 A position. Before energizing, coordinate the source-side protective device and secondary-feeder ampacity with both 100 A Blue Sea 2314 buses; this conductor/protection coordination is the remaining feeder warning.

No insulated secondary-enclosure feed-through studs are purchased. Route one protected positive feeder and one negative feeder through ordinary strain-relieved glands unless a stud pair is later selected and electrically and mechanically verified. Verify both purchased 32 A breakers, their 24 V conductors and every downstream terminal before energizing; separately confirm how the Orion current-limited 12 V output and retained socket harnesses protect the 12 AWG socket A→B daisy chain.

Use the canonical graph as the wiring authority: every physical device and conductor in the detailed diagram is the same object rendered in 3D. Resolve graph validation or A* routing failures in code; do not add hand-positioned glands, routing exceptions or undocumented wires.
